q: The ergodic decomposition theorem states that every invariant probability measure μ for a measurable transformation T can be decomposed as:
opts: μ = ∫ μ_x dμ(x) where μ_x is ergodic for μ-a.e. x
μ = Σ cₙμₙ for finitely many ergodic measures
μ is always ergodic for a generic T
exp: Ergodic decomposition: the space of invariant measures is a Choquet simplex with extreme points being the ergodic measures. Every invariant measure decomposes as a (possibly uncountable) integral/mixture of ergodic measures, unique for standard Borel systems.
